sources.citation: Roger N. Shepard, Jacqueline Metzler (1971). Mental Rotation of Three-Dimensional Objects. Science.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1971) in Science establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: Michael Peters, Christian Battista (2008). Applications of mental rotation figures of the Shepard and Metzler type and description of a mental rotation stimulus library. Brain and Cognition.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2008) in Brain and Cognition extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Tomoaki Kozaki (2022). Training effect on sex-based differences in components of the Shepard and Metzler mental rotation task. Journal of Physiological Anthropology.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2022) in Journal of Physiological Anthropology extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Stephen M. Kosslyn, Giorgio Ganis, William L. Thompson (2001). Neural foundations of imagery. Nature Reviews Neuroscience.
sources.notes: Establishes that mental rotation recruits superior parietal spatial maps alongside dorsal premotor motor-simulation circuitry.

sources.citation: Shenna Shepard, Douglas Metzler (1988). Mental rotation: Effects of dimensionality of objects and type of task. Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (1988) in Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance extending the foundational findings.
